entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
Software reliability and security, though related, are distinct concerns within the realm of Bitcoin development. The core protocol functions as the backbone of the entire network, meaning that any failure at this level can have widespread repercussions for all users. In contrast, wallet software operates at a more individual level, so issues here tend to be contained and affect fewer people.
Balancing the complexity between these two layers is a critical design decision. Increasing the sophistication of the core protocol in an attempt to preempt every possible mistake that could occur within wallet software adds overall complexity and risk to the protocol itself. As a result, it is often preferable to maintain a simpler, more robust core protocol even if this means accepting that wallet software may remain susceptible to certain classes of errors.
Ultimately, prioritizing the integrity and simplicity of the core protocol ensures greater overall reliability for the system as a whole. While failures in wallet software can result in loss of funds for individuals, systemic failures caused by protocol flaws would have far more severe consequences across the entire Bitcoin ecosystem. For further insights into this philosophy, refer to [Peter Todd’s website](https://petertodd.org).
